name: Male infertility due to acephalic spermatozoa

criteria.description: Presence of >90% acephalic (headless) spermatozoa on semen analysis
Exclusion of azoospermia or other causes of male infertility
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with acephalic spermatozoa (e.g., SUN5, PMFBP1)
History of primary infertility with normal secondary sexual characteristics

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of >90% acephalic spermatozoa on semen analysis plus exclusion of other infertility causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Normal serum testosterone and gonadotropin levels
imaging: Scrotal ultrasound typically normal or mild varicocele

distinguishingFeatures: Absent or defective acrosomal cap on sperm
Sperm motility defects due to ciliary dysfunction
Associated respiratory symptoms and situs inversus

redFlags: Absence of sperm head-tail coupling in >90% sperm
Failure to conceive after 12 months of unprotected intercourse
references: Kherraf ZE, et al. Acephalic spermatozoa syndrome: clinical, genetic, and molecular insights. Hum Reprod Update. 2018.
Sha YW, et al. SUN5 mutations cause acephalic spermatozoa syndrome. Am J Hum Genet. 2017.
Orphanet: Male infertility due to acephalic spermatozoa (ORPHA:529970)
